groups.defect: ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled (lines 192-195) throws UnsupportedOperationException, but the ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls it. Client deletion can therefore fail, and the per-client authorization resources are never cleaned up.

answer.reasoning: Both suggestions point at the same lines (192-195) in ClientPermissionsV2. Both report the same defect: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, and the client-removal listener in AdminPermissions calls it. As a result, client deletion breaks and the per-client resources are left orphaned. They also propose the same fix: make it a no-op, implement the cleanup, or change the listener. They disagree only on when the listener reaches the V2 path. s_85b8c9a1 says whenever the V1 feature is on. s_9201a4d6 says when both the V1 and V2 features are on. That is a difference in how they explain the trigger, not a different defect. s_9201a4d6 also mentions, as a secondary point, that cleanup is skipped in V2-only mode. It already covers everything s_85b8c9a1 says, including the orphaned resources, so one member's comment is enough and no unified comment is needed. That last call is a little debatable, but the grouping itself is clear.
